name: Pethuel
overview: Pethuel is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of the prophet Joel. The Scriptures identify him explicitly in this paternal role, though no additional tribal affiliation or other personal details are provided. His mention is concise, focusing on his relationship to Joel without further elaboration.
namesAndTitles: The name Pethuel means 'G-d’s opening,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's involvement or revelation. This proper name is recorded in Joel 1:1 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Pethuel is the father of Joel, the prophet, as stated in Joel 1:1. Beyond this paternal link, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pethuel's significance in the biblical narrative rests chiefly on his role as the father of Joel, a major prophet whose writings contribute to the Old Testament. Although Pethuel himself does not have a direct narrative or theological role, his identification establishes Joel’s lineage and grounds the prophetic message within a historical family context. This connection underscores the biblical pattern of prophetic ministry emerging within specific familial lines.
